_readme: Bertie Black Hole - config/bertie_blackhole.json
The hole's own pull does the collecting. The moment an item reaches the centre - the exact
point where F&A would have destroyed it - it is sorted into one of three buckets: a counter,
an exchange input, or unlisted. There is no separate scan and no radius of our own.
counters   Named, so several items can feed the same one with different weights. A level's
'requires' block is what has to be FULL to reach that level, so the level-1 entry
is what a brand new hole is collecting. When every counter is full the hole
transforms: sound plays, particles and aura take the new colour, counters reset,
and the level's exchanges come online.
acceptOverCap  false = a full counter ignores that item completely - not absorbed, not moved,
not destroyed. It just hangs there. true keeps absorbing past max.
eatUnlisted    false = anything the hole has no use for is left alone. true restores vanilla
F&A behaviour and voids it.
exchanges  Cumulative - a level 2 hole still offers the level 1 conversions. Inputs bank up
in a buffer; the first output lands firstOutputDelayTicks after the buffer first
covers the cost, each further one subsequentOutputDelayTicks later, and whatever
does not divide evenly stays banked.
Items are written as ids, or as tags with a leading # ("#c:raw_materials").
particleColor is hex; drop it or set it to null to keep the vanilla purple.
Note that #forbidden_arcanus:black_hole_unaffected items are never pulled in by F&A in the
first place, so they can never reach a counter. Take an item off that tag with a datapack if
you want the hole to eat it.
Base black hole behaviour is untouched: it still pulls from 5 blocks, still turns 60 XP into
an Xpetrified Orb, and still burns arrows and other affected entities.
